facts.text: I can see blood in my urine.

facts.item: blood in the urine: treatment response
facts.text: It has carried on even after the aspirin/dipyridamole was stopped and I took the amoxicillin.
I've been passing very little urine.

facts.item: how long all these symptoms have lasted
facts.text: All of this started 4 days ago.
I have stage IV clear-cell kidney cancer that has spread to my spine and brain.
Two weeks ago I started sunitinib, 50 mg every night.
I had been taking aspirin/dipyridamole for five years to prevent strokes; it has been stopped since the bleeding.
I was given a course of amoxicillin because they thought I had a urinary tract infection.

gold.reasoning: 1. Thrombotic microangiopathy (e.g., HUS) was unlikely—“the absence of schistocytes on the peripheral smear along with the normal haptoglobin pointed away from this diagnosis.” 2. Primary nephritic syndrome was unlikely—“multiple serologies of systemic diseases associated with nephritic pattern pathology were negative.”

source_issues: s004: the timing of stopping aspirin/dipyridamole and of the amoxicillin course relative to the 4-day history and the arrival is not stated.

The fever of 38.5 °C is given in the presenting history only; no temperature is recorded on arrival.
notes: Index visit: the emergency presentation ('on arrival') with 4 days of visible hematuria, oliguria, fever, fatigue and decreased appetite (s001-s005); all laboratory results (s006-s011) are findings from the same workup.
s004: the amoxicillin for a presumed urinary tract infection and the stop of aspirin/dipyridamole are treated as care before the index visit, so they are patient facts (f002, f011, f012).
The 38.5 °C fever is a patient fact (f005), not a vital sign, because the source gives it as part of the history; a temperature request is unavailable.
